subject: AI & Agents
title: OpenAI Five: Conquering Dota 2
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on OpenAI Five: Conquering Dota 2.

hook.text: Five AI agents coordinate in real time to defeat a professional Dota 2 team. The crowd roars.

buildup.text: Dota 2 is enormously complex — imperfect information, teamwork, long time horizons, and fast reflexes.

discovery.text: OpenAI Five trained by playing 180 years of game time per day using reinforcement learning.

twist.text: The bots developed strategies humans hadn't considered — sacrificing heroes early to gain advantages.

climax.text: This showed AI could handle teamwork and strategy in chaotic, real-time environments.

punchline.text: Five minds, one goal, zero egos. The perfect team was silicon.

quiz.question: What made Dota 2 a challenging test for AI?
options: It requires teamwork, strategy, and real-time decisions with imperfect information
It only involves simple pattern matching
It has a very small number of possible moves

details.summary: OpenAI Five defeated professional Dota 2 teams, mastering a game with long time horizons, complex teamwork, and over 100 playable characters — all through self-play reinforcement learning.
details.whyItMatters: Dota 2 requires team coordination and strategic planning over 45-minute matches. The achievement showed that reinforcement learning can handle long-horizon, multi-agent cooperative problems.
takeaways: OpenAI Five beat top professional Dota 2 teams
It mastered complex teamwork through self-play alone
Long-horizon planning with many variables was key challenge

faq.question: What made Dota 2 a significant AI challenge?
faq.answer: Matches last around 45 minutes with thousands of decisions, require five AI agents to coordinate as a team, and feature incomplete information. The strategic complexity dwarfs chess or Go.

faq.question: How much compute was needed to train OpenAI Five?
faq.answer: OpenAI Five trained for the equivalent of 180 years of gameplay per day using thousands of GPUs. The massive compute requirement highlighted both AI progress and its resource-intensive nature.
